name: @keke1933/vibe-dictionary-mcp

tools.name: search_techniques
tools.description: Search Korean/English names, aliases and use cases. The calling assistant must turn the relevant part of the user request into a short phrase for one effect or use situation. For example, rewrite "I need a mark showing my edits have not been saved" as "unsaved changes" or "저장 상태". The MCP does not generate keywords or run a language model. Search independent techniques separately, for example "minimal" with domain "style" and "bento grid" with domain "layout" in separate calls. Partial matches are ranked by coverage and field importance; unrelated words can exclude useful candidates. Names and aliases outrank prompts. Mandatory filters always apply. Use domain/category and optional target/trigger to narrow required properties. Start with limit 5. Nonempty queries return relevance order with score (not confidence) and matchedOn field names; empty query browses catalog order. Responses exclude full prompts. locale defaults to ko; use en for English output. Compare summaries and useCases with the original request. If results are empty or unsuitable, retry a synonym, the other language or fewer modifiers, and broaden only optional filters. Reset offset to zero for a changed query or filters. If candidates still do not fit, ask the user. Some demos simulate scroll/drag/audio using clicks/timers; check triggers and the original prompt.

query.description: Short Korean/English effect words, aliases or use situation generated by the calling assistant for one desired technique. Search independent techniques separately; omit to browse.

target.description: Required target type, e.g. button or card.

trigger.description: Required implemented demo input, e.g. pointer-move, click or drag.

locale.description: Output language; search matches both languages regardless of locale.

limit.description: Page size, maximum 50; use 5 for initial candidates.

tools.name: get_technique
tools.description: Get one technique by exact ID from search_techniques, with the original reference prompt in the selected locale (ko default, en supported), aliases and use cases. Before combining selected techniques, read each prompt and compare application areas, visual treatment, inputs and timing; search rank does not establish compatibility. Translation preserves inputs, timings and demo limitations. titleKo/titleEn retain both canonical names for compatibility. Returns reference text only; does not execute it or modify files. Unknown IDs return an error; search again.

locale.description: Output language; search matches both languages regardless of locale.

instructions: Find UI, graphics, layout, style and video techniques. Search for a few candidates, compare summaries, useCases and matchedOn fields, then get_technique by exact ID only for the selected prompts. The calling assistant interprets the user request and generates short Korean or English search phrases for one effect at a time. The MCP performs bilingual weighted keyword/alias matching and runs no AI model. Extract concrete effects and targets; omit uncertain filters. For broad requests such as a clean or premium webpage, use the stated purpose and preferences; do not equate an adjective with one fixed style. Ask for clarification when missing context prevents a meaningful choice. For requests combining techniques, search distinct needs such as style, layout and interaction separately. Retrieve the selected prompts, then decide where each technique applies and compare their visual treatment, inputs and timing for conflicts. The tools do not compose techniques or check compatibility; the calling assistant makes those judgments. Use target/trigger filters only for required demo inputs. Compare summaries and useCases against the original request. If candidates are missing or unsuitable, retry a synonym, the other language or fewer modifiers, and remove only filters that are not required. Reset offset to zero when changing the query or filters. Do not select an unrelated result merely because it ranks first; clarify if useful candidates still cannot be found. Scores are not probabilities. locale selects output language independently of search language. These read-only tools return reference data only.
